result:
All six fixes (F1, F2, F3, F5, F6, F8) are in, `node --test experiments/workflows/records-v3.test.mjs` passes 35/35 (21 before), and the live Haiku 5.5 dev check passes 10/10. I touched no git state and edited only the three permitted files. Two commits made by another process ("WIP snapshot" 70df598 and cfee56d) already contain my in-progress edits; I did not make them. The dirty files under `beds/` are not mine.

I found two further problems and fixed both:
- **F9 (extra, flagged):** `toE164` read a BRIGHTDESK local number whose digits begin 011 as the US access code, so `01 114 4194` became `+144194`. It showed up as a phone mismatch on d4 s160. The fix is at line 520 with a unit test; it is separable if you want it reverted.
- **A regression my own F3 rewording caused:** my first rewording of the "answer for the order BEFORE that change" sentence made both Haiku and Sonnet read a team's move ("moved from A to B") as the dated change, so the VENDEX date order was unresolved. In a supplementary pass on seeds 101-112 at d4, s108 and s109 failed because of it. The wording at line 966 now separates the two, and both seeds pass.

## What changed

All line numbers are in `/home/user/workflow-foundry/experiments/workflows/records-v3.mjs`.

- **F1 (merge join):**
  - `merge` is now `join: 'all_resolved'` (line ~1231). `vendex_diff` and `adjudicate` are added to its needs.
  - A handled atlas_switch error now gives the diagnostic `ATLAS switch judgment failed (<code>): no dated order change applied` (line 604), and the run still produces an answer.
  - I added the unit test and a scripted-provider test. A control test shows that with the old default join, merge, check and answer are skipped and the run ends in ACCEPTANCE_FAILED.
- **F2 (country adjudication):**
  - New helpers `vendexReadsOf` (301), `vendexCountryDispute` (316) and `combineVendexReads` (331).
  - The `vendex_diff` code node (`disputesMain`, 772) lists the rows where the reads disagree on country. A missing claim against a code counts as a disagreement. The adjudicator sees the entry and the stated places, but not the competing codes.
  - The `adjudicate` map node (1226) uses the extraction class, escalating to `maxClass`. It returns an ISO enum plus a verbatim quote; its instructions and checks are at 1148-1160 (checks reject `other` and an unquoted country).
  - Each adjudication is recorded in `merge.adjudications` and shown as a `note:` in the check. A failed adjudication leaves the first claim that has evidence and adds a diagnostic (lines 849-850).
- **F3 (prompts):** every example in the prompts is now synthetic, covering names, dates, phones, balances, places and country typos. I checked the new examples against dev seeds 101-160 at d3-d5. `ADJUDICATE_INSTRUCTIONS` is new. A unit test now bans the old literals.
- **F5:** the mirror-check window is 365 days (line 1054).
- **F6:** `COUNTRY_CHECKS` (1135) now enforces names and codes length equal to ids and rejects `none` as well as `other`. `merge` adds `unmapped country string` diagnostics (802) and reports a failed chunk with its string count (794).
- **F8:** `FIXED_STATUS` (118) is the one marker table. `VOID_MARKERS`, `LIVE_MARKERS` and `MARKER_ENUM` (127-131) are derived from it. `ISO3` (137) is the one alpha-3 map. Both reach the `prep` and `merge` code nodes through args (lines 1199, 1234), and `exactCountry` takes `iso3` as a parameter (459).
- **Dev driver** `records-v3-dev.mjs`: it now logs, prints and summarises `adjudications`.
- **Header comment** (line 98): updated with the results below.

## Tests

35 of 35 pass. The new tests cover:
- the dispute routing in `combineVendexReads` and `disputesMain`;
- `mergeMain` with adjudications, unmapped countries and a handled atlas error;
- the countries, adjudicate and mirror checks;
- the prompt-literal ban and the single-copy markers;
- the workflow shape and validity;
- the scripted-provider runs described under F1.

## Live dev results (Haiku 5.5, `--conv M --extract M --max L`, final code)

I did not use the labels you named. `h55fix-d3` and `h55fix-d4` were the first run, before the 011 fix and the date-prompt fix: 10/10 pass, with d4 s160 scoring 0.9987 on the phone bug. The numbers below are re-measured on the final code under labels `h55fix3-d3` and `h55fix3-d4`.

| difficulty | seed | pass | score | cost | calls | escalations | adjudications |

| d3 | 156 | yes | 1.000 | $0.0125 | 20 | 0 | 0 |
| d3 | 157 | yes | 1.000 | $0.0133 | 22 | 0 | 0 |

| d3 | 159 | yes | 1.000 | $0.0199 | 21 | 1 | 0 |
| d3 | 160 | yes | 1.000 | $0.0127 | 20 | 0 | 0 |

The d3 total is $0.072 and the d4 total is $0.080. The one escalation (d3 s159) was the statuses node going from M to L.

I also ran seeds 101-120 at both difficulties on the final code: 20/20 at d3 and 20/20 at d4, all scoring 1.000, with two escalations in total.

Disputes are rare. Across the 50 final-code runs there were 0 adjudications. The only live adjudication in 62 runs of the final code was d4 s106: read A said none, read B said CA, place "Regina", and the adjudicator returned CA with a verbatim quote. So the live evidence for the adjudicator is thin beyond that one case.

These are dev-seed results only, not held-out evidence. Total spend across all live runs was $1.43 of the $3 cap.

I did not update `README.md`, which is outside the permitted files.
